title: Severe External Bleeding Control
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid Guidelines 2020; American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS COT) Stop the Bleed Guidelines

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately and ensure the immediate scene is safe
Expose the wound: cut or push away clothing to see the exact bleeding source
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure directly over the bleeding point using sterile gauze, clean cloth, or bare hands if no dressing is available
Maintain direct pressure without lifting the dressing to check the wound; add more dressings on top if blood soaks through
If life-threatening bleeding on an arm or leg does not stop with direct pressure, apply a commercial windlass tourniquet 5 to 7 cm above the wound (never over a joint)
Tighten tourniquet until bright red spurting or heavy bleeding completely stops, secure the windlass rod, and record the exact application time
Keep the patient warm and lying flat to treat or prevent hemorrhagic shock

do_not: Do not remove or peel away dressings that have soaked through; always apply new dressings directly over existing ones
Do not remove a tourniquet once applied, even if bleeding has stopped; only trained medical personnel should release it
Do not apply a tourniquet directly over a joint (elbow, knee) or directly over an open fracture
Do not attempt to probe, clean, or remove deeply impaled objects from the wound
